title: Four Letters and a Hat Shop
summary: Bee the tapir wants four painted letters to put a new hat shop on the map. When her window spells NOPE just as Tansy tries the most spectacular hat in town, the shop needs a second answer.
coverAlt: Four Letters and a Hat Shop. Bee the striped-apron tapir faces a blue shop window. Moss, the slim greyhound milliner, balances a giant double-loop pink hat over the counter while Tansy the spectacled fox looks on.
style: Cut-paper pop screenprint in tomato, flamingo pink, chartreuse and cobalt, with tactile ink, chunky sign tiles and roomy speech balloons.

pages.alt: Bee the tapir brings four little painted tiles to the hat shop. Moss, a tall greyhound wearing a measuring tape, points her toward the empty shop window.
pages.transcript:
BEE
Four letters. A whole window. Finally, a job my size.

MOSS
Put up OPEN before the first customer grows another season of fur.

pages.alt: Bee admires her arrangement. The four painted blocks read PENO. Moss points at a solitary P perched on a hat stand.
pages.transcript:
BEE
PENO. Very stylish. What does it say to you?
PENO

MOSS
That the P has hired an agent.
P

pages.alt: Tansy, a russet fox in round glasses, arrives with a little hatbox. Moss shows her a modest cap beside a spectacular pink hat with two giant ribbon loops.
pages.transcript:
TANSY
I’ve come for a perfectly quiet hat.

MOSS
Quiet is two shelves down from unbelievable.

pages.alt: Tansy leans toward the pink hat while a squirrel and a pigeon watch from the street. Bee turns toward their expectant faces at the glass.
pages.transcript:
TANSY
Does that pink one come with a little less audience?

BEE
We’ve only got the one audience. They’re regulars.

pages.alt: Bee flourishes her hands over the window tiles. Moss holds a mirror while Tansy reaches toward the huge looped hat.
pages.transcript:
BEE
Watch this. I can make a window wink.

MOSS
You could make it spell OPEN. I hear that’s popular.

pages.alt: Tansy tries the pink hat at the window mirror. Bee completes the arrangement and everyone turns toward the sign, which reads NOPE.
pages.transcript:
TANSY
I think this one might be me.

BEE
There! Everybody look!
NOPE

pages.alt: Under the sweeping ribbon brim, Tansy frowns toward the shop window. Bee lifts both hands and tries to explain what she meant.
pages.transcript:
TANSY
That is a very big word for four little letters.

BEE
I was arranging the colors. I wasn’t answering you.

pages.alt: Seen from the pavement, Tansy is framed by the window, mirror and onlookers. Bee studies the fitting mirror standing right against the display glass.
pages.transcript:
TANSY
Then why did it feel like the whole window answered?

BEE
Because I put your mirror in the window.

pages.alt: The squirrel raises its paws and the pigeon waits for another flourish. Bee meets her audience at the door and asks for space.
pages.transcript:
SQUIRREL
Again! Make the letters dance again!

BEE
I finally got a crowd. Now I’m going to ask it for some room.

pages.alt: Bee and Moss position the oval mirror in a curtained alcove. Tansy raises the huge brim and peeks out with a new smile.
pages.transcript:
BEE
No votes on hats. Even very tall hats.

TANSY
What if I specifically request a gasp?

pages.alt: Tansy chooses Moss to admire the hat. Moss tips her long muzzle back in a tiny gasp while Bee keeps quiet.
pages.transcript:
TANSY
I’ll have a tiny one. From Moss.

MOSS
Oh!

pages.alt: Moss boxes the modest cap. Tansy wears the enormous pink one, and Bee gathers the four shop-window tiles.
pages.transcript:
TANSY
Box the little hat. This one’s taking me home.

BEE
I still owe the window an honest answer.

pages.alt: Moss gestures toward the shop window and fitting room. Bee turns one thick blue tile beside three paint pots, a brush and a small mirror that catches her smile.
pages.transcript:
MOSS
Which answer? Are we open, or are we voting?

BEE
That’s two questions. Good thing the letters have backs.

pages.alt: The squirrel looks in from the street at OPEN. On the other side of the very same window, Tansy reads NOPE from the colored backs of the four blocks.
pages.transcript:
SQUIRREL
Is the hat shop open?
OPEN

TANSY
And are strangers voting on my hat today?
NOPE

pages.alt: Tansy wears the pink double-loop hat out of the shop. She tips the brim and winks behind her round glasses, leaving Bee and Moss amused.
pages.transcript:
MOSS
I think that hat just winked at me.

TANSY
That was me. The hat’s still learning.
